note: Editorial shortlist. Route names identify a line of ascent, not turn-by-turn directions. Distances, times, tracks and summit elevations are intentionally omitted until independently checked.

peaks.name: Ben Nevis
peaks.summary: The familiar Glen Nevis ascent to Britain's highest summit; navigation can be serious in cloud or snow.

peaks.name: Ben Macdui
peaks.summary: A long high plateau journey to Britain's second-highest summit.

peaks.name: Cairn Gorm
peaks.summary: A high Cairngorm summit with exposed plateau terrain beyond the ski area.

peaks.name: Schiehallion
peaks.summary: A distinctive conical Munro with a maintained lower path and a rough quartzite upper ridge.

peaks.name: Ben Lomond
peaks.summary: A popular Loch Lomond summit day with a sustained climb above the eastern shore.

peaks.name: Buachaille Etive Mòr
peaks.route: Stob Dearg via Coire na Tulaich
peaks.summary: A steep ascent to the landmark pyramid at the entrance to Glen Coe.

peaks.name: Bidean nam Bian
peaks.summary: A big mountain circuit above Coire Gabhail with steep, rough ground.

peaks.name: Meall Dearg
peaks.summary: A committing, exposed ridge traverse for experienced scramblers.

peaks.name: Liathach
peaks.summary: A sustained Torridon ridge day with exposed scrambling choices.

peaks.name: An Teallach
peaks.summary: A celebrated sandstone ridge with exposed pinnacles and demanding route finding on the direct crest.

peaks.name: Stac Pollaidh
peaks.summary: A short but steep ascent with a dramatic Assynt panorama; the western summit needs scrambling.

peaks.name: Suilven
peaks.summary: A remote approach and steep final climb to an isolated sandstone landmark.

peaks.name: Ben Hope
peaks.summary: A remote northern Munro with broad views and a rough, steep approach.

peaks.name: Sgùrr Alasdair
peaks.summary: A steep, loose Cuillin ascent that demands mountain experience and careful navigation.

peaks.name: Scafell Pike
peaks.summary: The direct Wasdale ascent to England's highest summit crosses rocky mountain terrain.

peaks.name: Helvellyn
peaks.summary: A classic exposed ridge above Red Tarn with hands-on-rock sections.

peaks.name: Skiddaw
peaks.summary: A broad northern Lake District ascent on a well-known mountain path.

peaks.name: Blencathra
peaks.summary: A short but serious exposed crest where wet or windy conditions add risk.

peaks.name: Great Gable
peaks.summary: A rocky central fell reached from the well-known Sty Head pass.

peaks.name: Catbells
peaks.summary: A compact ridge walk above Derwentwater with a few rocky steps.

peaks.name: Haystacks
peaks.summary: A varied fell walk above Buttermere with rocky summit terrain and tarns.

peaks.name: Fairfield
peaks.summary: A long ridge circuit from Ambleside crossing several summits.

peaks.name: Bowfell
peaks.summary: A rough high fell reached from the Langdale side via Three Tarns.

peaks.name: Pavey Ark
peaks.summary: A classic rising ledge above Stickle Tarn with sustained exposure.

peaks.name: Kinder Scout
peaks.summary: An accessible approach to the Peak District's broad moorland plateau.

peaks.name: Pen-y-ghent
peaks.summary: A distinctive Yorkshire Three Peaks summit with a short steeper section.

peaks.name: Whernside
peaks.summary: A broad Yorkshire Dales ridge approached near the Ribblehead Viaduct.

peaks.name: Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon)
peaks.summary: The popular Llanberis approach to Wales' highest summit remains a challenging mountain day.

peaks.name: Tryfan
peaks.summary: A long, rocky ridge and one of Britain's best-known introductory scrambles.

peaks.name: Glyder Fawr
peaks.summary: A steep approach from Cwm Idwal to the rocky Glyderau plateau.

peaks.name: Glyder Fach
peaks.summary: A steeper scramble above Bwlch Tryfan onto Glyder Fach.

peaks.name: Cadair Idris
peaks.summary: A scenic southern ascent above Llyn Cau to the summit ridge.

peaks.name: Pen y Fan
peaks.summary: A popular Beacons summit approach on a clear path that is exposed to weather.

peaks.name: Cribyn
peaks.summary: A sharp summit on a longer ridge circuit in the central Beacons.

peaks.name: Y Garn
peaks.summary: A rocky ascent above Cwm Idwal with broad views across the Ogwen valley.

peaks.name: Moel Siabod
peaks.summary: A varied ridge from the Capel Curig side with scrambling that can be varied in difficulty.

peaks.name: Pen yr Ole Wen
peaks.summary: A steep route from the Ogwen valley to the Carneddau skyline.

peaks.name: Fan Brycheiniog
peaks.summary: A scenic approach from the lake to the western Beacons escarpment.

peaks.name: Slieve Donard
peaks.summary: A sustained ascent from Newcastle to Northern Ireland's highest summit.

peaks.name: Slieve Binnian
peaks.summary: A Mourne circuit passing Blue Lough and distinctive granite tors.

peaks.name: Zugspitze
peaks.summary: A long Alpine approach to Germany's highest summit, with exposed summit terrain.

peaks.name: Mulhacén
peaks.summary: A high-altitude Sierra Nevada walk to the Iberian Peninsula's highest peak.

peaks.name: Pico Ruivo
peaks.summary: A shorter signed route to Madeira's highest summit, with steep steps and rapid weather changes.

peaks.name: Mount Olympus
peaks.summary: A major mountain ascent whose final approach to Mytikas involves exposed scrambling.

peaks.name: Mount Fuji
peaks.summary: The best-known Fuji summit trail is a high-altitude ascent with a regulated climbing season.

peaks.name: Mount Kinabalu
peaks.summary: A guided summit trek through changing vegetation and high granite terrain.

peaks.name: Mount Takao
peaks.summary: A well-served woodland summit walk with an accessible transport connection from Tokyo.

peaks.name: Mount Monadnock
peaks.summary: A short but steep and rocky New England summit trail.

peaks.name: Mount Washington
peaks.summary: A steep White Mountains ascent where severe weather is possible in any season.

peaks.name: Half Dome
peaks.summary: A long Yosemite day ending at the cables; permits and seasonal access rules apply.

A serious exposed ridge where the modest technical grade does not describe the commitment.
A shorter rocky ridge alternative above Red Tarn, commonly linked with Striding Edge.
